anchor_text: Did Norges Bank kill the Omnibus? Not officially. But in practice, for most serious businesses, yes. While EU politicians debate dilution and exemptions to hashtag #CSRD and hashtag #CS3D through the hashtag #Omnibus proposal, Norges Bank Investment Management (NBIM) has raised its sustainability expectations for every company it invests in globally (link in comments). They are the world’s largest sovereign wealth fund and among the most influential shareholders globally. They manage over €1.5 trillion in assets and hold stakes in over 9,000 companies. When they set expectations, companies listen. And the market moves forward. They now require: 1. Clear board-level responsibility for sustainability. 2. Science-based targets for both climate and nature. 3. Human rights due diligence aligned with UNGP and OECD. 4. Transparent, forward-looking reporting aligned with hashtag #ESRS, hashtag #GRI, or hashtag #TCFD. NBIM’s expectations are, point for point, what the Omnibus proposal is trying to delay or weaken. And they’re not alone. The European Central Bank is also openly criticizing the Omnibus, warning that weakening CSRD risks undermining financial stability. So, here’s the reality. Even if the Omnibus passes, it has already been made largely irrelevant. In two years, even more so. Because the financial market is moving faster, and demanding more, than EU policymakers. Investor expectations take precedence over regulatory delays. And companies that want capital, clients, or credibility need to keep up. Norges Bank didn’t kill the Omnibus with a vote. They killed it with capital. Agree?
